image.name: LBCT LLC
image.description: LBCT LLC operates the automated Long Beach Container Terminal at the Port of Long Beach's Middle Harbor/Pier E complex. The approximately 300-acre marine terminal provides vessel, yard, gate and on-dock rail handling for trans-Pacific container trade and has more than 3.5 million TEU of annual capacity. Olivia Holdings LLC acquired 100% of LBCT in October 2019 for US$1.78 billion. The current investor group includes Macquarie Infrastructure Partners IV, Munich Re through MEAG, Manulife/John Hancock and Rest; only Munich Re's 8.8% Olivia Holdings interest is publicly quantified, so the other consortium stakes remain explicitly undisclosed.

image.name: Pinsly Railroad Company
image.subsector: Short-line freight rail and rail logistics
image.description: Pinsly Railroad Company is a U.S. short-line freight-rail and logistics platform operating nine railroads across ten states. The business provides freight transportation, transload, railcar storage, industrial-development, warehousing and related logistics services to customers in agriculture, chemicals, fuels, plastics, building materials, lumber and metals. Macquarie Infrastructure Partners V acquired 100% of predecessor RailUSA in 2022. The platform later operated as Gulf & Atlantic Railways, acquired the legacy Pinsly railroad and logistics businesses in 2023, and adopted the Pinsly name in 2024. The operating railroads and logistics subsidiaries are components of this single manager-level platform.

image.subsector: Infrastructure-adjacent road-marking and engineered glass materials
image.description: Potters Industries, LLC manufactures glass beads, microspheres and engineered materials used in road and airfield markings and specialized industrial applications. image.description: TraPac, LLC operates marine container terminals in Los Angeles and Oakland serving ocean carriers, truckers, rail providers and cargo owners moving containerized freight through the U.S. West Coast. Lines and Brookfield Asset Management are former owners. TraPac Jacksonville transferred separately to Ceres in 2022 and is excluded from this platform boundary.

image.name: Yusen Terminals LLC
image.description: Yusen Terminals LLC operates a marine container terminal at the Port of Los Angeles on Terminal Island. Its infrastructure includes berths, cargo-handling cranes, storage yards, gate systems, on-dock rail and shore-power facilities serving container lines and North American import and export supply chains. Ocean Network Express acquired NYK's 51% interest in 2023 and subsequently became the terminal's sole owner after Macquarie Infrastructure Partners III sold its separate 49% interest for US$550 million. The exact closing date and buyer vehicle for Macquarie's later sale were not publicly disclosed.

image.name: Maverick 6 & 7
image.description: Maverick 6 & 7 is a shared California renewable-power portfolio comprising the Maverick 6 solar-plus-storage project and the Maverick 7 solar project in Riverside County. Maverick 6 includes 100 MWac of solar generation and a 50 MW / 200 MWh battery system, while Maverick 7 provides 132 MWac of solar generation. Munich Re, through a MEAG-managed MR Falcon vehicle, owns 50% of each project and EDF Renewables retains the other 50%. The projects operate within CAISO and supply contracted renewable power; their project LLCs are treated as underlying assets rather than separate portfolio companies.

image.description: TowerPoint Infrastructure Partners is a U.S. wireless-infrastructure platform that acquires, owns, and manages towers, easements, rooftops, and related telecom real estate for wireless carriers and other network operators. TowerPoint Capital manages the platform; its direct equity participation is not publicly disclosed and is not recorded as ownership.
